title: Polk County School Board, District 3 (runoff)
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school millage, hire and evaluate the superintendent, approve curriculum materials, and set district policy.
verified_ballot_note: Runoff per LkldNow (https://www.lkldnow.com/school-board-elections-district-3-heads-to-run-off-fields-and-sharpless-cruise-to-victory/) and The Ledger/Yahoo. Nonpartisan.

education_choice.summary: Wallace says she has been open about her support for robust school choice, and her campaign site says she worked in Tallahassee for statewide public school choice and for expanded scholarships for students with unique abilities, and helped bring IDEA Public Schools charter schools to Lakeland. She lists empowering parents with more quality options among her top three priorities.

other_issues.title: Reading instruction and screen time
other_issues.summary: Wallace says schools must commit fully to the science of reading and adopt only evidence-based, high-quality instructional materials, with intensive reading intervention. She also says screen time for the youngest learners should be little to none.

candidates.name: Victor Sims
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Sims, 30, is a senior program officer whose career has been in child and family advocacy and social work. He is a former foster youth from Polk County who says he attended 12 schools, and he is the parent of a child with an individualized education plan. He holds degrees from Polk State College, the University of South Florida, Florida International University and Florida State University's law school, and finished second in the August 2026 District 3 primary.
